steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with a silicon mat or parchment paper.
Mash the butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a large mixing bowl with a spatula until creamy and smooth, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla; whisk vigorously for 20 to 30 seconds.

Whisk the flour, salt, and baking soda together in a small bowl; dump into the butter mixture and mix until just combined. Fold the semi-sweet chocolate chips, white chocolate chips, and milk chocolate chips into the mixture. Arrange onto the prepared baking sheet using a small scoop or large spoon.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 10 minutes; remove from oven and allow to cool on the sheet for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling completely.

review.reviewBody: These turned out absolutely perfect. I made this with my two boys this morning so we could bring a random act of kindness to their babysitter. We only made one change and that was upping the vanilla to a full teaspoon. I didn't really measure the chips out, I just used the random amounts I had in each bag that I had leftover from other cookies. I made no other changes. These turned out wonderfully. We baked the cookies at 350 degrees and they were done in exactly ten minutes. The boys really liked the different chips in this cookie and it was great for me because I could use up the little bits I had in my cupboard in each chip bag PLUS it made the perfect amount--neither too much or too little. This recipe's a keeper.

Good base recipe. I made a few adjustments to my batch. 
(I doubled the recipe)
I reduced the butter by a few tablespoons. I added 1/4 cup of cocoa powder, and 1 cup each of white chocolate and milk chocolate. I used 1 cup of brown sugar and 1/4 of white sugar for a double recipe. 
I whipped my eggs, butter, sugar and vanilla together for about 5 minutes to get it extra fluffy. 
I also chilled the cookie dough in the fridge for about 15 minutes before balling onto pan. 
Search #jezzaskitchen for photos

Great recipe, but I changed some things. First, 375 degrees was too much, so I changed it to 350 for better results. I also melted the butter a little bit in the microwave, and the cookies turned out fine. Another thing I did with the cookies was that I split the dough in half and added about 1/8 of a cup of unsweetened cocoa powder and 1/8 cup of white sugar to make chocolate cookies. Whatever you do with these cookies, don’t bake them with a greased up baking sheet(I just use wax paper)

I have made this recipe multiple times, and it is actually incredibly easy and are probably the most delicious cookies I have ever eaten.

I add 1/2 a cup of each chocolate chip type.
Great recipe! I adapted and added mini candy coated pieces instead of the milk chocolate chips. I also added an extra 3/4 cup of Reese chips. Turned out amazing!!!

My 17 year old gobbles these up as fast as I can make them. They're delicious as-is, but I sometimes substitute oats for half the flour (I always use whole wheat) and often times add a big scoop (4 TB or so)of creamy peanut butter, just to change it up a little. Once when we were out of butter I used applesauce instead, and he didn't even notice the difference; I think the peanut butter masks the applesauce flavor. As you can see it's a great recipe as written but also versatile!

So easy and fantastic recipe. It was a little sweet and buttery to me first time, so I omitted 1/4 cup brown sugar and instead of using white sugar I used 1/2 cup brown sugar. Also I cut the butter to half for the 2nd time and it was wonderful. I am going to make it again this morning. :)
We added walnuts and used a 1/2 cup of chips instead of a 1/3. These cookies were absolutely amazing!!!

Excellent! I used about two and a half (3.5oz) chocolate bars chopped, ranging from bittersweet to 70% chocolate. I made 17 cookies which took about 15 min to bake to golden perfection at the recommended 375 deg F. Cookies were delicious, crispy golden around the edges, slightly soft and chewy on the inside.

I tried this recipe and I think it is good. Still searching for the ultimate. I will be using this one until then. I don't like white chocolate so I put in 2/3 c milk choc chips and 2/3 cup semi sweet chips. I think it was just a few too many chips. otherwise, not bad.

I didn't really realize how few cookies it made until I started. One cookie sheet using a cookie scoop. I went with milk chocolate, semi minis and white using the recommended 1/3 cup. Less salt since my butter was salted. It took 15ish minutes and they spread very nicely. They turned out a bit browner than I like so I will go with 13-14 min in my oven. My daughter wants 4.5 stars -even tho they have the dreaded semi-sweet chips.
Very good! I only had white chocolate and milk chocolate chips. they were sweet (semi sweet chips may have made them less sweet) with delicious cookie dough. Good texture. Will make again.
When I made these cookies, my whole family loved them!
very sweet, typical chocolate chip cookies; small batch
I always suck at making cookies, but this recipe is legit! No guess work needed. My cookies came out beautiful.

My son chose this recipe for a class cookie exchange. I had never made this recipe before, but made it as written. We did not care for this cookie. The batter thins out in the oven and spreads pretty quickly, so I would recommend dropping them by the 1/2 tsp fulls. I dropped by 1 tsp fulls first batch and baked for 10 minutes and the cookie was thin and crispy and over baked imo, so the second batch I limited to 8 minutes and they were still really brown. If you like thin, crispy cookies to dip in milk then you will like this cookie. Very thin and crispy for sure. They did have a nice buttery flavor. Not sure how chewy they will be in the morning, might be even MORE crunchy. I am going to place a brown sugar bear in his container to hopefully maintain some moisture. I would recommend decreasing the temperature to 350 and see if that helps?
I like it
Cookies spread and came out super flat. Don’t know what I did wrong.
No changes yes will make again

I have to make these almost weekly because of how good they are. My brothers fight over who gets the most and ask me to make them for their birthday presents. The only thing that I have changed is adding an extra bit of almond extract, though that is from personal preference and is not needed. Follow the recipe and you should have the best chocolate chip cookies you will ever taste.
